summary: Julia Ching was a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied at the College of New Rochelle, Catholic University of America, and Australian National University, later teaching at Columbia and Yale before becoming a professor at the University of Toronto in 1978.

Julia F. Andrews is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at Brown University, the University of California, Berkeley, and Harvard University, and held a post at Ohio State University around 1987.
Julia Leslie worked in Indology and religious studies. She founded SOAS University of London and held a post there from circa 1993 to 2004.

Juliane Schober is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989 and was an associate professor of religious studies at Arizona State University (attested 2007).
Julie Gifford specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds and held a post at Miami University.

Julius Eggeling was an Indologist who studied at the universities of Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served at the Royal Asiatic Society, University College London, and as professor at the University of Edinburgh (1875–1914).

Julius Euting worked in linguistics and history/archaeology, studying at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He held librarian posts in Tübingen, became an honorary professor at the University of Strasbourg (1880), and directed its National and University Library.

Julius Grill was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Urach, Tübingen, and Jena under Rudolf von Roth and Adalbert Kuhn. He taught at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren seminaries and served as professor of Old Testament exegesis at Tübingen (1888–1913).

Julius Hoffory was a linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen, Frederick William University Berlin, and the University of Strasbourg. He held a post at Frederick William University Berlin from circa 1883 to 1890.

Julius Jolly was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin, Munich, and Leipzig under Albrecht Weber and Martin Haug. He completed his habilitation at Würzburg, where he was a professor (1877–1920), and was Tagore professor at Calcutta (1882–1883).

Julius Lipner is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Jnana Deepa, Jadavpur University, and King's College London under Hywel David Lewis. He taught at the University of Birmingham before becoming a professor at the University of Cambridge (1975–2013).
Julius Pokorny was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Rudolf Much at the University of Vienna. His academic posts included Vienna, Berlin (1920–1935), Bern, Zurich, and Munich.

Julius Schubring was a scholar in history and archaeology. He pursued his studies at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, the University of Bonn, and the University of Göttingen between 1857 and 1862.

Julius Zupitza was a linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Moriz Haupt. He held academic posts at the University of Breslau, the University of Vienna, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1876–1895).
Jun Fujii is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo (1999–2005) and served as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University from circa 2009 to 2013.

Jun Takashima is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara. He held posts at JSPS, Aichi Prefectural University, Toyo University, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, where he became a professor.

Jundo Nagashima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seitatsu Matsunami, Alexis Sanderson, and Paul Williams (earning a PhD at the University of Bristol), and has held posts at Taisho University and its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute.

June McDaniel is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Emory University and the University of Chicago. She has served as a professor in religious studies and taught philosophy and religion at the College of Charleston.

Junglan Bang is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Seung-suk Jung, Sungdoo Ahn, and Harunaga Isaacson, completing degrees at Dongguk University and the University of Hamburg (PhD, 2012), and served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed a master's degree at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and earned a PhD at Duke University under Stanley Abe.
